description: Run a SQL query against your schema in an ephemeral PostgreSQL (pglite, in memory) before you hand it over, instead of guessing whether a column exists: does it run, which columns it returns with their real PostgreSQL types, how many rows, a small sample — or Postgres's own error with its SQLSTATE and position. Runs inside a transaction that is rolled back, so an UPDATE or DELETE is safe to check. Give `compareWith` (e.g. a reference query, or the version before your rewrite) to check both return the same rows: they are also run on adversarial data (NULLs, duplicates, empty tables), and if they differ you get the smallest counter-example with its INSERT statements — the classic NOT IN with a NULL.

compareWith.description: Optional second read-only query that should return the same rows

ordered.description: With compareWith: also compare row order (only if ORDER BY matters)

schema.description: CREATE TABLE … plus INSERTs with some sample data. Can be empty

name: db_query_check
